findings.evidence: The proof uses only `integrable_const C` (finite measure), `Integrable.mono'`, `hf.aestronglyMeasurable` and a compact-interval bound; nothing Gaussian is used.
findings.fix: State it for arbitrary `ρ` with `[IsFiniteMeasure ρ]` and arbitrary centre `c`, move it to a general MeasureTheory integrability file, and apply it here at `gaussianReal μ v`.
findings.issue: `integrable_of_integrable_sub_smul_gaussianReal` is general infrastructure (continuous f, integrable (x - c) • f under a finite measure implies f integrable) but is stated only for `gaussianReal μ v` with centre μ and placed in the Gaussian IBP file.

findings.evidence: Proof: `rw [gaussianReal_of_var_ne_zero μ hv, integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul' ...] at hg; simpa only [toReal_gaussianPDF]`. Grepping mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/Distributions/Gaussian for integrable lemmas finds only `integrable_exp_mul_gaussianReal` and `integrableExpSet_*`.
findings.fix: Replace it with the iff `integrable_gaussianReal_iff_integrable_gaussianPDFReal_smul (hv : v ≠ 0) : Integrable g (gaussianReal μ v) ↔ Integrable (fun x => gaussianPDFReal μ v x • g x)` and use `.1` at the call sites.
findings.issue: `integrable_gaussianPDFReal_smul_of_integrable` exports only the forward implication, although its proof rewrites with the iff `integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul'`. The converse (density-weighted Lebesgue integrability implies integrability under `gaussianReal μ v`) is missing, and Mathlib has no such lemma.

summary: The integration-by-parts surface is sound, but a general finite-measure integrability lemma is exported in Gaussian-specific form and file, and the density-integrability lemma exports only one direction of the iff its proof already establishes.
